question: Do the few occupied pilot sources of ultrarare mammals divide the heldout island network into distinct source-influence territories, rather than behaving as spatially redundant copies?

source_influence.paths: full frozen island graph; occupied sources are endpoints, unoccupied islands may be traversed
source_influence.target_support: targets with positive total kernel access from at least one focal occupied source

diversity_partition.alpha_effective_sources: 1 / mean_t(sum_s p_ts^2), equally weighting supported heldout targets
diversity_partition.gamma_effective_sources: 1 / sum_s(mean_t p_ts)^2, equally weighting supported heldout targets
diversity_partition.interpretation: beta > 1 indicates spatial turnover in which different targets depend on different source subsets; high beta together with high local dominance is distributed irreplaceability

preserves: exact source count in each bioregion
matched_random_placement_null.sampling_frame: pilot islands in matching bioregions, without replacement
matched_random_placement_null.primary_descriptive_contrast: actual beta_source_turnover minus species-specific null mean

claim_boundary: no heldout occurrence values may be read
do not call low occupancy a temporal range contraction
do not infer extinction filtering, refugial selection or realized dispersal
do not infer temporal insurance or persistence from spatial source turnover
do not use this diagnostic to rescue BALA or upgrade the mammal evidence class
do not select a new occupancy threshold

interpretive_fork.if_beta_actual_gt_null: few observed sources divide target space more strongly than matched random placements; topology specificity is compatible with distributed irreplaceability rather than source clustering
interpretive_fork.if_beta_actual_not_gt_null: existing complementarity result reflects global leverage balance without evidence for target-space division of source influence
